technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Given an existing turn that PersistTurn/upsert and queryHistory succeed against, POST .../dialog with at least one valid dialog item returns HTTP 200 and totalDialogCount increases by the posted item count.

- A non-InvalidOperationException from AppendProcessingDialogAsync (for example DbUpdateException) is returned as a classified session-log error (not_found, persistence_error, validation_error, or backend_unavailable) rather than HTTP 500 with error=internal_server_error.
- When appendDialog fails, current-turn.yaml auditDialog is unchanged from before the call.
- After a failed appendDialog, a later successful completeTurn does not leave local auditDialog higher than the server-side processing dialog count for that requestId.
Implementation notes:

- SessionLogController.AppendDialogAsync only catches InvalidOperationException and maps 'not found' to 404. Other exceptions fall through to GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware as opaque internal_server_error. Widen the catch and use ClassifiedError, matching the RequirementsController BUG-TRIAGE-073 pattern.

- AppendProcessingDialogAsync uses raw SaveChangesAsync. Submit/Replace/Upsert used by PersistTurn use SaveChangesBudgetedAsync. Keep dialog persist on the same save/classification path as those sibling mutations.

- plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog increments auditDialog before Invoke-ReplRaw client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync. Move the increment after success, or roll it back on failure. Failsafe currently queues only timeout/503, so a 500 drops the dialog items.
- Do not treat local current-turn.yaml status=completed plus auditDialog as proof the incremental dialog POST persisted.
description: workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog is intercepted by Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog and calls client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync (POST /mcpserver/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/dialog -> SessionLogController.AppendDialogAsync -> AppendProcessingDialogAsync). That path returned method_invocation_error wrapping McpServerException with internal_server_error. The extracted error string matches GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware (payload.error=internal_server_error), not the controller ClassifiedError envelope, so an exception other than InvalidOperationException escaped AppendDialogAsync. appendActions, updateTurn, and completeTurn succeeded because they persist via Invoke-ReplPersistTurn (full session SubmitAsync/upsert), and queryHistory succeeded against the same cache, so the session/turn existed. Plugin still incremented current-turn.yaml auditDialog before the server call and did not roll it back; completeTurn then left local status=completed with auditDialog=3 even though the dialog POST failed.
BUG-TRIAGE-165.title: appendDialog POST returns internal_server_error while sibling session-log writes succeed

BUG-TRIAGE-170.note: S0: drain timeout stays under FR-MCP-REPL-011 and TR-MCP-REPL-012. Current Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds default is REPL_FAILSAFE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT 120. Proof-only. Do not mark done until H-done AGREE.
technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- workflow.failsafe.drain replaying client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync must use a timeout at least as large as the non-drain SubmitAsync budget (REPL_TIMEOUT, or a dedicated drain timeout), not a hardcoded 2 seconds.

- A failsafe SessionLog record whose SubmitAsync completes within the configured drain timeout must be replayed and removed from the live queue, not aborted with 'backend unreachable: mcpserver-repl timed out after 2s'.
- An explicit workflow.failsafe.drain of a payload that succeeds outside drain (observed ~73s with REPL_TIMEOUT=90) must not classify that latency as backend unreachable.

- Automatic/nested drain must still avoid blocking an in-flight getFr/getTr caller for a long SubmitAsync (preserve TR-MCP-PERSIST-003 via deferral or an equivalent non-blocking path, not a 2s timeout that cannot succeed).
- A timeout abort during drain must leave drainAttempts unchanged so a later successful pass can still replay the record.
Implementation notes:

- The smoking gun is Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds: if ($script:ReplFailsafeDraining -and $Method -eq 'client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync') { return 2 }. Both Invoke-WorkflowFailsafeDrain and Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrainOnFirstSuccessCore share Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrain, so the cap hits operator drain and automatic drain.

- Do not reuse the 2s cap as the nested-drain safety valve. ReplRawInFlight / ReplFailsafeDrainDeferred already defer drain so it does not sit inside getFr/getTr. Raise or remove the drain-specific SubmitAsync timeout and keep that deferral.

- Default non-drain timeout is still 30s unless REPL_TIMEOUT is set. Observed successful submit was 73s, so drain should use REPL_TIMEOUT, REPL_HELPER_TIMEOUT, or a dedicated REPL_FAILSAFE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT large enough for real session-log payloads.
- Test-ReplFailsafeBackendUnreachable matching 'timed out' is correct for a true transport failure; the bug is the artificial 2s budget producing that timeout on a reachable backend.
description: workflow.failsafe.drain sets ReplFailsafeDraining, then Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 returns a hardcoded 2 seconds for client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync. Invoke-ReplRawCore kills the REPL after that budget and returns 'mcpserver-repl timed out after 2s'. Test-ReplFailsafeBackendUnreachable treats 'timed out' as backend unreachable, so the pass aborts after one record and leaves drainAttempts at 0. The same payload submitted outside drain with REPL_TIMEOUT=90 completed in 73s. The 2s cap was meant to keep a nested drain from blocking getFr/getTr (TR-MCP-PERSIST-003), but it also applies to the operator drain verb and to deferred automatic drain, so live SessionLog failsafe records cannot replay.
BUG-TRIAGE-170.title: Failsafe drain hardcodes a 2s SubmitAsync timeout and aborts the queue

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Sequential client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync of real failsafe session_submit payloads does not return HTTP 503 backend_unavailable while the process is up and /health remains Healthy with storage reachable.
- When SaveChanges hits lock, busy, or the 5s StorageCommandBudget without a connection-class outage, the response is not backend_unavailable (busy/retryable persist, not storage-down).

- workflow.failsafe.drain replays a session_submit that takes longer than 2s (observed 73-88s, leftover 76s) without aborting as backend-down and without leaving the YAML stranded after storage answers.

- A 503 backend_unavailable burst leaves failsafe YAML on disk and a later in-process drain with storage answering replays it (no drainAttempts increment, no completed latch, no quarantine for this abort).
- /health nonce echo and overall Healthy stay as liveness-only; if writes are 503 because storage is actually down, the health payload storage field is unreachable.
Implementation notes:

- Do not treat this as BUG-TRIAGE-167 / SQL error 19 classification. Observed code is backend_unavailable (StorageCommandBudgetExceededException, RetryLimitExceededException, or connection-class SqlException), returned by SessionLogController.ClassifiedError or GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware.

- Root overlap with sessionlog-remediate-001 RC1/RC4: plugin still POSTs a full UnifiedSessionLogDto; SessionLogService.FindExistingSessionAsync is unbounded; only SaveChangesBudgetedAsync is 5s. Prefer incremental persist (AppendDialogAsync) and/or busy-timeout/retry over raising the 5s budget blindly.

- Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds returns 2 when $script:ReplFailsafeDraining and Method is client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync (TR-MCP-PERSIST-003: do not block getFr/getTr). Large records must drain on a long-timeout background path, not the 2s in-request walk.

- FR-MCP-FAILSAFE-001 / FR-MCP-SESSIONPERSIST-002 already require 503 degrade-queue and drain retry after storage answers; this incident is the live proof that 2s drain plus full-session upsert cannot meet that.
description: Out-of-band replay of Grok session_submit failsafe YAML (drain hardcodes a 2s SubmitAsync timeout in Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds while ReplFailsafeDraining) posted 41 records, many taking 73-88s, then 11 consecutive client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync calls failed with method_invocation_error HTTP 503 code backend_unavailable starting 2026-08-21T14:56:02Z. /health later echoed a nonce and stayed Healthy (TR-MCP-HEALTH-003 liveness; storage-only faults do not flip overall status). Remaining YAML stayed on disk until a later 120s-timeout replay succeeded (first leftover 76s for GrokCode-20260818T182741Z-plugin-session, then 1s). This is a live write-path burst, not the SQL error 19 classifier gap. SubmitAsync still full-graph upserts (FindExistingSessionAsync loads turns/actions/tags/dialog/commits unbounded; only SaveChangesAsync is under StorageCommandBudget 5s). Budget expiry and RetryLimitExceededException map to retryable backend_unavailable, so slow or contended saves look like storage-down while liveness stays Healthy. Drain cannot self-heal these payloads.
BUG-TRIAGE-171.title: SessionLog SubmitAsync 503 burst after large failsafe replay; 2s drain cannot recover

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Replaying 20260722T232406Z-session_submit-3358.invalid-requestid-corrupted-shape.yaml through client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync succeeds (map-shaped turns are converted to a list before deserialize, or submit accepts the repaired payload).

- Replaying 20260817T123057Z-session_submit-d5f9.yaml and 20260817T123219Z-session_submit-9ad7.yaml succeeds without HTTP 400 validation_error Invalid session turn planFile/todoId: planFile is omitted.
- After successful replay, those three files are no longer left in F:\GitHub\McpServer\.mcpServer\codex\failsafe\quarantine.
- A failsafe drain of remaining Codex session_submit quarantine files does not leave these three records stuck after DrainAttempts with the same deserialize or omitted-planFile rejection.
Implementation notes:

- 3358 payload: params.sessionLog.turns is YAML mapping key "0" with only requestId; UnifiedSessionLogDto.Turns is List/ICollection of UnifiedRequestEntryDto, which requires a JSON array. Repair on drain by converting object-keyed turns to an ordered list; do not loosen the live DTO contract unless a compatibility converter is explicitly chosen.

- d5f9 and 9ad7 payloads: turns is a one-item array with requestId req-20260817T104212Z-prompt-6212 but no planFile or todoId. Validator in src/McpServer.Services/Services/SessionLogTurnContextValidator.cs requires both on new persist; allowed sentinel is exact value None. Prefer drain-time injection of None for historical failsafe records over weakening live submit validation.
- Do not delete the three quarantine files until they post successfully or are moved to an explicit terminal archive state.
- August files currently show lastDrainError internal_server_error after later replay; the on-disk payloads still omit planFile/todoId, which remains a hard validation failure for new-entry submit.
description: After 167 successful Codex failsafe SessionLog.SubmitAsync replays, three files remain in F:\GitHub\McpServer\.mcpServer\codex\failsafe\quarantine and still reject. 20260722T232406Z-session_submit-3358.invalid-requestid-corrupted-shape.yaml stores turns as a string-keyed map ("0") instead of a sequence, so SubmitAsync cannot deserialize sessionLog.turns to List<UnifiedRequestEntryDto>. 20260817T123057Z-session_submit-d5f9.yaml and 20260817T123219Z-session_submit-9ad7.yaml have list-shaped turns but omit planFile and todoId; SessionLogTurnContextValidator.ValidateForNewEntry rejects omitted planFile. DrainAttempts already exceeded; later replay still fails. Files were not deleted.
BUG-TRIAGE-172.title: Repair three unpostable Codex failsafe SessionLog.SubmitAsync quarantine records

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- Failsafe drain of session_submit queues does not POST *.importRecovery.yaml envelopes through client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync.
- A dedicated import-recovery replay walks {workspace}/.mcpServer/{agent}/failsafe/pending/<rootId>.<sourceHash>.importRecovery.yaml documents whose root key is importRecovery.
- Replay persists from yamlArtifactPath and/or sourceFiles (re-ingest Persist=true or ITranscriptSessionPersister.PersistAsync), not by treating the envelope as a UnifiedSessionLogDto.
- On persisted=true and degraded=false the matching pending envelope is deleted; on persist failure the file stays in failsafe/pending.
- Successful replay of the two named Codex pending files removes those files from Codex/failsafe/pending.
Implementation notes:
- Writer: TranscriptRunArtifactWriter.WritePendingAsync and CreateRecoveryEnvelope in src/McpServer.SessionLog.Transcripts/TranscriptRunArtifactWriter.cs.

- Delete-on-success: TranscriptIngestionService.PersistPendingAsync in src/McpServer.SessionLog.Transcripts/TranscriptIngestionService.cs; persister maps the transcript session then calls ISessionLogService.SubmitAsync on the DTO, not the envelope.
- Plugin drain: Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrain in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 requires method+params and only scans Get-McpFailsafeDir; it does not scan failsafe/pending.

- Do not reuse workflow.sessionlog.importRecovery as the envelope drain unless it first loads yamlArtifactPath into a UnifiedSessionLogDto. That API currently merge-submits session logs, not importRecovery envelopes.
description: Codex transcript persist writes write-ahead envelopes at {workspace}/.mcpServer/{agent}/failsafe/pending/<rootId>.<sourceHash>.importRecovery.yaml with root key importRecovery (runId, agent, workspacePath, rootId, sessionId, sourceKind, sourceHash, persisted, degraded, status, yamlArtifactPath, compatibilityArtifactPath, sourceFiles, diagnostics). Plugin failsafe drain only replays client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync session_submit records from Get-McpFailsafeDir. After that drain, 019d6472-5ba7-77d0-9b90-ee0d3f99599a.3fe421946dfc1353.importRecovery.yaml and 019d6481-c77a-74b3-8bd7-103167e0e0bb.b8611bc5364bf417.importRecovery.yaml remain because they are not method/params SubmitAsync records. Envelope deletion happens only in TranscriptIngestionService.PersistPendingAsync after ITranscriptSessionPersister.PersistAsync reports success. There is no drain that reads leftover pending envelopes and re-invokes transcript persist.
BUG-TRIAGE-173.title: Codex pending importRecovery YAML has no replay path besides SessionLog.SubmitAsync

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- When workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn persist via client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync times out or returns HTTP 503/backend_unavailable, the call still reports queued/degraded, retains the session_submit failsafe, does not throw, and returns success so the agent can continue.

- After that degrade, current-turn.yaml for the same requestId stays status=in_progress and still contains the fields already written for the turn (queryTitle, queryText, planFile, todoId, openedAt, and audit counters). Degrade must not replace the file with a three-field stub.
- A later successful persist or failsafe drain of that retained session_submit record writes the same requestId with the original planFile and todoId.
Implementation notes:

- Do not treat the SubmitAsync timeout/503 itself as the TODO. Invoke-ReplPersistTurn already classifies timeout|timed out|command_timeout|backend_unavailable|HTTP 503 as degraded/queued and keeps the failsafe. Do not raise the default 30s sessionlog timeout (BUG-TRIAGE-072 hang risk).

- Fix Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1: if current-turn.yaml already exists for that requestId, leave it (or merge status=in_progress). Only write a minimal identity file when the turn file is missing.

- Incident context: original workspace F:\GitHub\LyftAuditTools, Grok plugin, request req-20260822T141800Z-001-continue-plan-completion, TODO PLAN-ANDROIDALIGN-001. Failsafe replay was correctly deferred.
description: Grok plugin workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn for req-20260822T141800Z-001-continue-plan-completion hit the designed failsafe-queue path: client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync timed out or returned HTTP 503/backend_unavailable, so persist returned queued/degraded, the session_submit failsafe was kept, and the agent continued PLAN-ANDROIDALIGN-001. That timeout/503 mapping in Invoke-ReplPersistTurn is the FR-MCP-SESSIONPERSIST-002 contract, not a new persist defect. The product bug is Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist: after Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn already wrote the full current-turn.yaml (queryTitle, queryText, planFile, todoId, openedAt, audit counters), the degrade helper Set-Content overwrites that file with only turnRequestId, sessionId, and status=in_progress. Later append/complete in the same session then persist from a stripped cache.
BUG-TRIAGE-175.title: beginTurn degrade path clobbers current-turn.yaml after SubmitAsync timeout

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- After user-prompt-submit reports turn-opened for a requestId, either the session store contains that turn or the hook does not report turn-opened; a queued/degraded beginTurn must be surfaced as degraded rather than a durable open.

- When current-turn.yaml is in_progress for a requestId that the store does not have, workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog must not return HTTP 404 not_found with failsafe refused. It must recover by persisting the missing turn then appending, or retain a replayable failsafe envelope, and the dialog items must not be lost.
- A Codex prompt-submit that logs beginTurn queued/degraded followed by appendDialog must still produce durable dialog (store or failsafe) for that requestId.
Implementation notes:

- plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1 Open-PluginTurn reports turn-opened after beginTurn exit 0 and current-turn.yaml matching the new requestId. It does not inspect LastReplPersistenceDetails.degraded/queued.

- plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn writes current-turn.yaml, then Invoke-ReplPersistTurn. Timeout/503 sets degraded queued failsafe-queue and Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist returns ok=true with current-turn left in_progress, so beginTurn returns true.

- Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog uses incremental POST client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync. Combined output matching not_found|HTTP 404 logs 'turn not found (retryable false); failsafe not used' and returns false without Write-ReplFailsafe. Timeout/503 is the only appendDialog failsafe path.

- Fix at the seam: do not advertise a store-backed open until SubmitAsync (or failsafe drain) creates the turn; and/or on appendDialog 404, re-submit the cached turn then retry dialog (or queue a combined failsafe) instead of refusing persist.
description: user-prompt-submit (Open-PluginTurn) treats workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn as success when persist is queued/degraded. beginTurn writes current-turn.yaml before SubmitAsync, then returns true on timeout/503 while the failsafe session_submit envelope is retained and the turn never lands in the session store. The hook still emits status turn-opened for that requestId (example req-20260904T022234Z-prompt-36ed). Later workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog posts client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync against the cached requestId, gets HTTP 404 not_found, and explicitly skips failsafe (retryable false). Incremental audit dialog is dropped even though the local turn remains in_progress.
BUG-TRIAGE-180.title: Codex prompt hook reports turn-opened for a store-missing requestId

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin CompleteTurn (workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn) succeeds against an in_progress current-turn.yaml that has turnRequestId and session metadata but no queryText key (or an empty queryText value).

- The completed persist payload includes a non-empty queryText recovered from cached queryTitle, or a recovered placeholder when both queryText and queryTitle are missing, and does not fail with a QueryText ParameterBindingValidationException.
- After CompleteTurn succeeds, the cached turn is no longer in_progress, so a later beginTurn or CompleteTurn does not keep operating on the stale requestId.
- Superseding that same queryText-less in_progress turn from beginTurn still persists the prior turn as canceled instead of dropping the persist with the same empty-QueryText bind failure.
Implementation notes:

- Failure site: plugins/core/lib-ps/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 CompleteTurn -> plugins/core/lib-ps/final-response.ps1 -> Invoke-WorkflowCompleteTurn in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1. Upsert builder is New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest in plugins/core/lib-ps/McpPluginShim.psm1 (QueryText is Mandatory, Title already has AllowEmptyString).

- Get-ReplCurrentTurnQueryText returns '' when the key is absent and Invoke-ReplTurnUpsertParams does not fall back to cached queryTitle. Align that recovery with SessionLogWorkflow.NormalizeTurn (FirstNonEmpty(QueryText, QueryTitle) then 'Recovered session-log turn').
- Keep TR-MCP-REPL-015 title omission on CompleteTurn. Recovered text belongs on queryText, not as a forced queryTitle rewrite.
- Cover the missing-queryText CompleteTurn and supersede paths in PluginPowerShellRuntime tests; existing fixtures always seed queryText so this gap is untested.
description: Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin CompleteTurn routes through final-response.ps1 to workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn. That path omits queryTitle unless the caller supplies it (TR-MCP-REPL-015), then Invoke-ReplTurnUpsertParams fills QueryText from Get-ReplCurrentTurnQueryText and falls back only to that empty title. New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest still marks QueryText Mandatory without AllowEmptyString, so a leftover in_progress current-turn.yaml with no queryText is rejected at bind time instead of being closed. beginTurn always writes queryText, so this is a stale or partial cache document (for example after an independent review). The failed close leaves the in_progress turn in cache, so later work can attach to the wrong turn. The C# SessionLogWorkflow already recovers QueryText from QueryTitle or 'Recovered session-log turn'; the plugin persist path does not.
BUG-TRIAGE-181.title: Codex CompleteTurn fails when current-turn.yaml lacks queryText

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- After a native sessionlog_begin_turn with planFile and todoId, Invoke-McpPlugin workflow.sessionlog.appendActions persists the supplied actions onto that same sessionId and requestId.
- appendActions must not rewrite current-turn.yaml sessionId from one *-plugin-session id onto a different *-plugin-session id when a native in_progress turn already exists.

- The persist payload for an in_progress append must include the existing planFile and todoId, or the server must preserve omitted planFile/todoId on incremental upsert instead of returning HTTP 400 validation_error planFile is omitted.
- The same native in_progress turn must accept both native sessionlog_dialog and plugin appendActions without failsafe session_submit 400s.
Implementation notes:

- Fix plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowAppendActions: pass PlanFile and TodoId from current-turn cache (or bind to the native in_progress sessionId/requestId) before Invoke-ReplPersistTurn.
- Assert-ReplCurrentTurnFresh sessionId rebind (TR-MCP-PLUGIN-012) is the observed plugin-session rotation; do not rebind away from a native in_progress turn.

- New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest in McpPluginShim.psm1 only emits planFile/todoId when non-empty; SubmitAsync in SessionLogService always ValidateForNewEntry except canceled superseded hook persists that stamp None.
- Prefer an incremental turn-append path (actions POST/upsert) over full-session SubmitAsync so omitted planFile cannot clobber or reject an already begun turn.
description: Invoke-McpPlugin workflow.sessionlog.appendActions does not persist against a native in_progress turn. Assert-ReplCurrentTurnFresh rebinds current-turn.yaml sessionId from the cached plugin session to the active session-state.yaml id (observed GrokCode-...015431Z-plugin-session to GrokCode-...055228Z-plugin-session). Invoke-WorkflowAppendActions then calls Invoke-ReplPersistTurn without PlanFile or TodoId; New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest omits blank planFile/todoId; client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync still runs SessionLogTurnContextValidator.ValidateForNewEntry, which 400s with planFile is omitted unless status is canceled. Native mcpserver sessionlog_dialog to the real session/request succeeded, confirming the plugin cache is a separate *-plugin-session identity rather than the native turn.
BUG-TRIAGE-182.title: Plugin appendActions rebinds plugin-session and SubmitAsync omits planFile

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Given current-turn.yaml exists with status in_progress and queryText omitted or empty, workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn exits 0 and does not throw ParameterBindingValidationException or invalid_parameter for queryText.
- When cached queryText is empty, the SubmitAsync turn payload omits queryText so the server preserves any previously persisted QueryText instead of writing an empty string.
- Pester covers updateTurn against an in_progress cache with empty or omitted queryText and an omitted title, including the persist payload shape.
- Plugin status continues to report the same active turn after a successful updateTurn.
Implementation notes:

- Mirror Title handling in plugins/core/lib-ps/McpPluginShim.psm1 New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest: add AllowEmptyString to QueryText and include queryText on the turn object only when it is non-whitespace.

- In plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Get-ReplCurrentTurnQueryText / Invoke-ReplTurnUpsertParams, fall back cache queryText then cache queryTitle before using the Title argument; if still empty, omit queryText rather than sending ''.
- Do not send queryText: '' on incidental re-submits. SessionLogService.UpdateEntryFromDto treats a present empty string as an explicit value and would clobber a stored QueryText.
- Cover the shared Invoke-ReplPersistTurn path so completeTurn, appendActions, failTurn, and supersede do not fail the same empty-cache bind.
description: workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn reports an active current-turn.yaml but then rebuilds a full client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync upsert. Invoke-ReplTurnUpsertParams reads cache queryText and, when that is empty, falls back only to Title. updateTurn omits Title per TR-MCP-REPL-015, so QueryText is passed as an empty string into New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest, whose QueryText parameter is Mandatory without AllowEmptyString. That bind fails before persist. Native REPL updateTurn does not require queryText, and the server already preserves omitted turn fields (FR-SUPPORT-015). Plugin status can still show the turn as active, so required model-authored session logging is blocked while the rest of the plugin looks healthy. The same persist helper is used by completeTurn, appendActions, failTurn, and supersede.
BUG-TRIAGE-184.title: Codex updateTurn rejects active turn when cached QueryText is empty

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn on a plan-backed in_progress turn persists status completed with the same planFile and todoId that beginTurn stored (or None when none was supplied) and stop-gate.ps1 no longer returns decision:block for missing plan metadata.
- workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn and appendActions persist without dropping planFile/todoId; current-turn cache still has those fields after a successful append or update.

- Incomplete cached turns and preserved failsafe records (including req-20260908T140505Z-prompt-c4b5 and the 20260908T225559Z / 20260908T225747Z session_submit files) can be reconciled through the supported sessionlog persist/drain path without deleting shared cache audit entries or marking the cache terminal.
Implementation notes:

- In plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1, read planFile and todoId from current-turn cache (written by Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn) and pass -PlanFile/-TodoId into Invoke-ReplPersistTurn from Invoke-WorkflowCompleteTurn, Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn, Invoke-WorkflowAppendActions, Invoke-WorkflowFailTurn, and Invoke-ReplSupersedeCurrentTurnIfInProgress.

- If cache lacks the fields, default to None the same way beginTurn does for a new turn; do not rely on empty-string defaults. Empty values are omitted from New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest, so the server never receives the required metadata on later upserts.

- Keep the beginTurn reopen path that omits unbound PlanFile/TodoId so a reopen cannot clobber server values; that omit-to-preserve behavior is not a substitute for complete/update/append, which must send the cached values.
- Reconcile the saved incomplete plugin-session turns via supported persist/failsafe drain only. Do not wipe shared cached audit state or mark it terminal as part of the fix.
description: Codex plugin workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn, updateTurn, and appendActions persist through Invoke-ReplPersistTurn without PlanFile/TodoId. beginTurn stores those fields on current-turn cache and passes them on first persist, including the 'None' default. completeTurn (repl-invoke.ps1 ~2011-2013), updateTurn (~1967-1969), appendActions (~1811-1813), failTurn, and supersede omit them. PersistTurn then defaults both to empty strings (~1250-1251) and still forwards them (~1270). The upsert DTO omits blank values, so later operations neither send the required metadata nor recover it from cache. That matches the TruckMate stop-gate block (completeTurn failed, turn left in_progress) and the identical child append failure, while a separate native sessionlog_submit that included planFile and todoId succeeded. This is a plugin payload/cache-closure defect, not an MCP outage. Shared cached audit must be reconciled, not erased.
BUG-TRIAGE-185.title: Plugin complete/update/append omit required planFile and todoId

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- When current-turn.yaml holds an auto-opened req-*-prompt-* id and appendActions is invoked with an explicit alternate requestId, the plugin either persists that explicit requestId or refuses the call; it must not submit the cached id.

- An additive appendActions persist for an in_progress turn includes the same planFile and todoId already stored on that turn (cache and/or params), so SessionLog.SubmitAsync does not return HTTP 400 'planFile is omitted'.
- appendActions returns success only after durable persistence is confirmed; a 400, throw, or non-persisted/degraded result must be a failed invoke with the failsafe retained.
Implementation notes:

- Mirror completeTurn requestId handling in Invoke-WorkflowAppendActions: read params requestId and refuse when it differs from current-turn.yaml turnRequestId, unless an explicit retarget path is added.

- Pass cached (or params) planFile and todoId through Invoke-ReplPersistTurn on additive in_progress submits. Empty-string omission is valid for queryTitle (TR-MCP-REPL-015) but not for planFile/todoId.
- Check Invoke-ReplPersistTurn's persisted result before returning true; do not treat a swallowed false/degraded persist as success.
- Do not weaken SessionLogTurnContextValidator.ValidateForNewEntry; the server rejection is correct. Fix the plugin payload and target selection.
description: workflow.sessionlog.appendActions in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 always persists Get-ReplTurnCacheField turnRequestId and never reads an explicit params requestId. completeTurn already refuses a mismatch; appendActions does not. technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Given current-turn.yaml with sessionId A, in_progress requestId R, and session-state.yaml with a different post-restart sessionId B, workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog persists dialog against session A and request R, not session B.
- current-turn.yaml sessionId remains A after appendDialog when R was created under A and still exists on the server.
- appendDialog does not return HTTP 404 / not_found for a recovered requestId that still exists on the original session.
- Marker-path or marker-timestamp drift (wrong workspace) is still rejected and does not persist against the recovered turn.
Implementation notes:

- The destructive rewrite is in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Assert-ReplCurrentTurnFresh: a sessionId-only mismatch logs a re-bind and writes current-turn.yaml sessionId to the active session-state.yaml value before any persist call.

- Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog calls Assert-ReplCurrentTurnFresh first, then Get-ReplSessionMeta, which uses Get-ReplCompleteTurnPersistSessionId on the already-rebound turn value, so persist always targets the new session.
- Same freshness gate is used by appendActions, completeTurn, and updateTurn, so the 404 is not unique to appendDialog.

- TR-MCP-PLUGIN-012 was written for Start-PluginSession rotation of an unbound local cache; recovered persisted turns after restart need the opposite policy: keep the original sessionId, or restore session-state.yaml from current-turn.yaml instead of minting a new session.
- The appendDialog 404 path already treats not_found as non-retryable and does not write failsafe, so the rebound cache is left pointing at a session that cannot accept R.
description: After a server restart, current-turn.yaml can still hold an in-progress requestId on the pre-restart session while session-state.yaml has a newly minted sessionId. Assert-ReplCurrentTurnFresh (TR-MCP-PLUGIN-012) treats that as session rotation and rewrites current-turn.yaml sessionId to the new session before persist. workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog then POSTs AppendDialogAsync with the new sessionId plus the old requestId and fails HTTP 404 because that requestId does not exist on the new session. Get-ReplCompleteTurnPersistSessionId already prefers the current-turn sessionId, but the freshness rewrite runs first and makes that helper see only the rebound id.

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- After MCP and subscriber recovery, workflow.sessionlog.appendActions on a recovered in-progress turn persists the submitted actions and returns success.

- When subscriber commit rejects or times out, the session-log graph remains at the pre-append snapshot (rollback completed) and the caller receives the coordinator failure reason rather than a generic unclassified internal error.
- Subscriber-unavailable and commit-timeout outcomes from session-log append/submit are classified as retryable backend/transaction failures (not HTTP 500 internal_server_error with retryable=false).
- A later appendActions after subscriber recovery succeeds on the same recovered in-progress turn without requiring a process restart solely to clear the prior commit rejection.
Implementation notes:

- Call path: workflow.sessionlog.appendActions -> src/McpServer.Repl.Core/SessionLogWorkflow.cs SubmitCurrentStateAsync -> POST sessionlog SubmitAsync -> TransactionGatedSessionLogService operation sessionlog.submit.
- Coordinator message is produced in TurnTransactionCoordinator after CommitDiffgramAsync; ToTransactionException in TransactionGatedSessionLogService appends 'Rollback completed.'
- McpErrorClassifier treats generic InvalidOperationException as internal_server_error/500/retryable=false; transaction rejections need structured classification (reason, retryable, status).
- Keep existing TEST-MCP-161 rollback compensation; add coverage for recovered in-progress appendActions after subscriber recovery and for classified retryable commit-failure responses.
description: workflow.sessionlog.appendActions persists through REPL SessionLogWorkflow.SubmitCurrentStateAsync into sessionlog.submit. TransactionGatedSessionLogService gates that submit through TurnTransactionCoordinator. After the local session-log mutation, CommitDiffgramAsync rejects any non-committed/non-duplicate subscriber result as 'Subscriber commit failed.', rolls back the pre-append graph, and throws InvalidOperationException. SessionLogController.ClassifiedError maps that exception through McpErrorClassifier to HTTP 500 internal_server_error with retryable=false, so recovered in-progress turns cannot durably append actions even after MCP recovery. Rollback itself matches TEST-MCP-161 fail-closed compensation; the defect is that a known subscriber-commit rejection blocks audit logging and is misclassified as a non-retryable internal error.
BUG-TRIAGE-199.title: Session-log appendActions returns HTTP 500 and rolls back after subscriber commit failure

BUG-TRIAGE-200.note: S0: rollback wording is superseded by effective FR-MCP-173. Ordinary sessionlog.* writes bypass the coordinator. Closeout is proof. Do not mark done until H-done AGREE.
technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- A supported workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog call against an existing in-progress turn with at least one valid dialog item returns HTTP 200 and the items remain queryable on that turn.
- A valid dialog append must not return HTTP 500 with detail containing 'Subscriber commit failed' and 'Rollback completed'.

- If subscriber commit is unavailable or times out after a valid local append, the API returns a retryable 503 (or equivalent classified retryable envelope) rather than non-retryable internal_server_error, and a later replay or retry persists the same dialog items.
- Concurrent valid session-log and other gated mutations in the same millisecond must not reject a valid appendDialog as a stale/duplicate subscriber sequence after the local mutation succeeded.
- A prior subscriber commit failure must not latch the coordinator into degraded mode that causes later valid appendDialog calls to fail without attempting persist.
- True invalid or unauthorized mutations still fail closed and roll back; only valid incremental dialog appends must persist.
Implementation notes:

- Server path: SessionLogController.AppendDialogAsync -> TransactionGatedSessionLogService.AppendProcessingDialogAsync (operationName sessionlog.dialog, MissingSnapshotRollbackPolicy.RestorePreMutation) -> ITurnTransactionCoordinator.ExecuteAsync. Post-mutation Failure() always sets Message 'Subscriber commit failed.' ToTransactionException appends 'Rollback completed.' when RollbackSucceeded.

- Do not hide commit.Reason. Surface StaleSequence, CommitTimeout, SubscriberUnavailable, hash/decrypt failures in the classified envelope so 503 retryable vs 400/409 vs 500 can be distinguished. McpErrorClassifier currently falls through InvalidOperationException to HTTP 500 retryable=false.

- Replace scoped unix-millisecond NextSequence() with a process-wide monotonic sequence (or keyserver-issued sequence) shared by all TransactionGated* adapters. Subscriber last-sequence is per publisher/subscriber pair across all operations, not per turn.

- Keep compensation for genuinely rejected commits, but a valid incremental dialog persist should not be undone solely because subscriber ack failed; either commit the dialog and retry subscriber evidence, or return retryable degrade without deleting the accepted items.

- Plugin: plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog already uses client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync. Align failsafe/replay with the classified retryable persist path so HTTP 500 rollback is not a silent drop and is not confused with triage failsafe YAML.
description: workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog for an existing turn posts incrementally to POST /mcpserver/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/dialog. With turn transactions required, TransactionGatedSessionLogService gates that as sessionlog.dialog: the local dialog mutation is saved, then TurnTransactionCoordinator subscriber commit is required. Any non-committed/non-duplicate commit result rolls the turn graph back and throws InvalidOperationException 'Turn transaction coordinator did not commit sessionlog.dialog ... Subscriber commit failed. Rollback completed.' SessionLogController.ClassifiedError maps that to HTTP 500 internal_server_error with retryable=false. The actual TransactionFailureReason (StaleSequence, timeout, subscriber unavailable, hash mismatch) is not returned. Per-request millisecond sequences on scoped gated services can collide on the singleton publisher/subscriber cursor after the row is already saved. A degraded latch then blocks later session-log writes. Plugin Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog only queues a session_dialog failsafe on timeout/HTTP 503, so a 500 drops valid model-authored dialog instead of persisting or replaying it.
BUG-TRIAGE-200.title: Valid sessionlog appendDialog returns HTTP 500 after subscriber commit rollback

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Given a trusted Codex plugin session with an in-progress current-turn.yaml, workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn persists the same requestId through client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync with process exit 0 and does not leave a new session_submit failsafe as the only durable copy.

- After that updateTurn, session-log GET/query for the same sourceType, sessionId, and requestId returns the updated response, interpretation, tags, and contextList from server storage, matching current-turn.yaml.

- When the turn-transaction subscriber rejects after a successful local session-log upsert of an existing in-progress turn, the plugin does not report persist failure while current-turn.yaml is already updated, and the operator is not left with failsafe-only copies of a locally accepted update.
- Repeating updateTurn for the same requestId is idempotent: live query still shows one updated turn and the failsafe queue does not grow on the success path.
Implementation notes:

- Named path: plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn writes current-turn.yaml via Write-ReplCurrentTurnState, then Invoke-ReplPersistTurn writes a client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync failsafe and calls the REPL child. Non-timeout/non-503 failure throws; updateTurn catches and returns false, which the Codex wrapper surfaces as persist failure.

- PersistTurn always submits a one-turn UnifiedSessionLogDto (turnCount=1). Server SubmitAsync is the full-session upsert, not UpsertTurnAsync. sessionlog-remediate-001 left updateTurn on that full upsert.

- src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Services/TransactionGatedSessionLogService.cs gates sessionlog.submit. RestorePostMutation applies only when no pre-image exists (create). An existing-session upsert uses RestorePreMutation, so subscriber reject rolls the server back while the plugin cache already moved forward. TEST-MCP-161 covers create-style restore; add coverage for updateTurn/upsert of an existing in-progress turn.
- Live Mcp:TurnTransactions RequiredForMutations is already known to break some sessionlog_begin_turn calls via keyserver/subscriber; the same gate applies to SubmitAsync used by updateTurn.
description: The trusted Codex plugin path for workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn writes the turn into current-turn.yaml first, then Invoke-ReplPersistTurn failsafe-queues and calls client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync. That REPL child exits 1, so the plugin keeps the session_submit failsafe and does not confirm live persist. This repeats the TEST-MCP-161 subscriber-rollback class: TransactionGatedSessionLogService.SubmitAsync mutates locally, then a subscriber/keyserver reject throws after rollback. For an existing in-progress session the rollback policy restores the pre-mutation graph, so the local cache is ahead of authoritative storage while PLAN-GIGMERGE-001 work continues.
BUG-TRIAGE-202.title: Codex updateTurn persist fails after local cache write

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Given plugin Status reports an active session and current turn, sequential wrapper invokes of workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog, appendActions, and updateTurn must each return a structured result that states whether that call persisted, queued to failsafe, or failed, including method name and failsafe path when queued.

- A failed or timed-out session-log wrapper must not end only with 'Plugin command failed with exit code 1'. Timeout and HTTP 503 cases must emit a classified retryable envelope (command_timeout or backend_unavailable), including stderr/persist details, matching the existing outer Invoke-McpPlugin timeout classification.

- workflow.sessionlog.appendActions must not report success when Invoke-ReplPersistTurn returns false or leaves a failsafe record. Local current-turn audit/cache updates must not be treated as durable persistence.

- After a mixed batch, workflow.failsafe.status pendingCount must be reconcilable to the named methods that queued, and a later Status/get of the same turn must make it observable which of dialog, actions, and turn fields were durably stored versus only queued.
Implementation notes:

- plugins/core/lib-ps/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 (non-zero ExitCode throw): stop collapsing inner REPL failures into a stdout-only generic throw. Emit a YAML error envelope that includes stderr and LastReplPersistenceDetails when present.

- plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowAppendActions: honor the Invoke-ReplPersistTurn boolean; do not `$null =` the result and return true. Delay or revert local audit increments until persist confirms, matching the appendDialog post-accept increment (BUG-TRIAGE-165).

- Keep per-call inspectability. appendDialog uses client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync; appendActions and updateTurn use full SubmitAsync upserts that write failsafe first. Do not present the three wrappers as an atomic batch unless a real batch API is added. Failsafe SubmitAsync payloads may omit dialog items already accepted by AppendDialogAsync, so drain/retry must not blindly resubmit a later upsert over a successful earlier dialog write.
description: With plugin Status showing an active session and turn, sequential Codex wrapper calls to workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog, appendActions, and updateTurn can run about 66 seconds and surface only 'Plugin command failed with exit code 1'. Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 throws that message from the child exit code and attaches stdout only, so stderr diagnostics from repl-invoke.ps1 are dropped. Inner session-log REPL calls use a 30s default timeout (Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds), which is below the 90s outer plugin timeout, so the already-classified outer command_timeout path does not fire. appendActions and updateTurn persist through Invoke-ReplPersistTurn, which writes a failsafe record before client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync and keeps it on timeout; that matches failsafe.status rising from 27 to 29. appendActions ignores the persist result and still returns success, while updateTurn returns false and exits 1. appendDialog uses a separate AppendDialogAsync path. The caller cannot tell which of the three writes persisted, queued, or only updated local turn cache, so retry and drain are unsafe.
BUG-TRIAGE-204.title: Codex session-log wrappers fail with generic exit 1 after partial persist

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- After beginTurn persist fails as degraded or queued, current-turn.yaml must not cause later appendDialog to POST incremental dialog against a requestId the server never stored.

- appendDialog against that ghost turn must not return false with 'turn not found (retryable false); failsafe not used' and must either create the turn (SubmitAsync or equivalent), replay the retained beginTurn failsafe then append, or queue a dialog/session failsafe.
- After that recovery, a following appendDialog or completeTurn on the same requestId succeeds without a manually written failsafe file.
- A genuine appendDialog to a requestId that was never opened locally still classifies as not-found, retryable false, and does not write failsafe.
Implementation notes:

- plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1: Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn writes the turn file then Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist keeps it when Test-ReplBeginTurnDegradedQueued is true; Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog lines 1891-1893 refuse failsafe on not_found/HTTP 404.
- src/McpServer.Services/Services/SessionLogService.cs AppendDialogAsync throws InvalidOperationException 'Entry not found: {sourceType}/{sessionId}/{requestId}' when no turn row exists.

- Do not weaken FR-MCP-170's true-missing-turn 404 rule. Gate the recovery on locally active/degraded current-turn.yaml (or a persisted=false marker) so only the ghost-turn path falls back to create-or-failsafe.

- Pester already locks degraded beginTurn cache retention (TriagePluginIdentity BeginTurn.SubmitTimeoutAfterFailsafe_ReturnsDegradedQueued). Add a follow-on case: degraded beginTurn then appendDialog must not take the 404 no-failsafe branch.
description: Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn writes current-turn.yaml before the server commit. When persist fails as degraded/queued, Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist keeps that cache in_progress and beginTurn returns success (FR-MCP-171). The next workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog then calls client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync because the cache file exists (FR-MCP-170). SessionLogService throws Entry not found for the never-committed requestId, which surfaces as HTTP 404. Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog matches not_found/HTTP 404 and explicitly skips Write-ReplFailsafe (retryable false). Session logging stays stuck on a ghost turn until an operator writes a supported failsafe by hand. The 404 classifier is correct for a truly missing turn; the defect is treating a degraded local cache as a durable server turn.
BUG-TRIAGE-205.title: Degraded beginTurn caches an uncommitted turn; appendDialog 404 refuses failsafe

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- When workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn persist is queued or degraded, user-prompt-submit must not return status turn-opened for a requestId the server does not own.
- current-turn.yaml must not remain status in_progress for a requestId that later appendDialog or appendActions will reject with HTTP 404 Entry not found.

- appendDialog after a degraded beginTurn must retain the submitted dialog items locally (failsafe or merge into the existing session_submit payload) instead of failing retryable false with failsafe not used.

- A later session-log update for that requestId must either succeed against a durable server turn or stay queued until the beginTurn session_submit failsafe drains; it must not present a false active-turn state.
Implementation notes:

- Root seam is plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn: Write-ReplCurrentTurnState happens before persist; Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist then returns ok=true degraded=true and beginTurn returns true with stderr queued/degraded.
- plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1 Open-PluginTurn only checks LastPluginReplExitCode and current-turn.yaml requestId, so it emits turn-opened without reading degraded or failsafe state.

- Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog uses client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync; SessionLogService.AppendProcessingDialogAsync throws Entry not found when the turn was never submitted. The 404 branch currently refuses failsafe by design; timeout/503 is the only appendDialog path that queues session_dialog.

- Preferred fix: do not advertise turn-opened until SubmitAsync confirms the turn, or keep a local degraded turn and route later appends through SubmitAsync failsafe merge instead of AppendDialogAsync. TEST-MCP-TRIAGEPLUGIN-001 BeginTurn.SubmitTimeoutAfterFailsafe_ReturnsDegradedQueued currently encodes keeping current-turn.yaml and will need to change with the contract.
description: Codex user-prompt-submit maps a degraded workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn to status turn-opened. Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn writes current-turn.yaml as in_progress before SubmitAsync, then returns success when persist times out or returns HTTP 503 with a retained session_submit failsafe. Open-PluginTurn treats that as a durable open because the REPL exit code is 0 and current-turn.yaml matches the requestId. The next workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog calls AppendDialogAsync, SessionLogService throws Entry not found for that sessionId/requestId, and the plugin classifies HTTP 404 as non-retryable with failsafe not used. Model dialog is dropped unless the caller manually enriches the original session_submit failsafe.
BUG-TRIAGE-208.title: Do not expose a locally active turn after degraded beginTurn the server cannot update

BUG-TRIAGE-210.note: S0: rollback wording is superseded by effective FR-MCP-173. Ordinary sessionlog.* writes bypass the coordinator. Closeout is proof. Do not mark done until H-done AGREE.
technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- A valid workflow.sessionlog.appendActions call on an existing in-progress turn persists those actions on the server turn after a durable commit.

- If sessionlog.submit is rejected by the transaction subscriber after the local mutation, the client-visible failure is retryable and does not leave the server turn missing the appended actions once failsafe replay succeeds.
- GET of the same sourceType/sessionId/requestId after recovery includes the appended actions, and the failsafe payload is cleared only after that durable write.
- Local current-turn cache must not report the turn as current when the server rolled back the append.
Implementation notes:
- Confirm the failure on TransactionGatedSessionLogService.SubmitAsync (operationName sessionlog.submit) and SessionLogController.SubmitAsync catch of InvalidOperationException via ClassifiedError.

- appendDialog already uses incremental client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync (sessionlog.dialog). appendActions still full-session submits a one-turn payload via Invoke-ReplPersistTurn; consider routing appends through sessionlog.upsert_turn instead of sessionlog.submit.

- Plugin path: plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowAppendActions updates cache then Invoke-ReplPersistTurn; HTTP 500 is not in the timeout/503 failsafe-queue branch, so the throw keeps FailsafePath.

- Subscriber-unavailable is an existing TransactionFailureReason; tests already expect rollback plus InvalidOperationException with Rollback completed. The product defect is that a routine action append becomes a stale-turn 500 rather than a committed incremental write or a retryable queued persist.
- Do not change fail-closed transaction policy without an equivalent retry/replay that restores turn currency.
description: workflow.sessionlog.appendActions persists through Invoke-ReplPersistTurn as a full-session POST to /mcpserver/sessionlog (client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync). TransactionGatedSessionLogService wraps that write as operation sessionlog.submit. When the turn-transaction subscriber rejects the post-mutation commit, the coordinator rolls back the session graph and SubmitAsync throws InvalidOperationException. SessionLogController.ClassifiedError maps that to HTTP 500. The plugin writes a failsafe payload before the call and does not treat HTTP 500 as the retryable 503/timeout queue path, so the exception is thrown and the failsafe file is retained. For an existing session, rollback restores the pre-mutation graph, so the appended actions never stay on server truth and the active turn is not current until that failsafe can replay. Local turn-cache audit counters are incremented before persist, so cache and server diverge after rollback.
BUG-TRIAGE-210.title: appendActions 500: sessionlog.submit subscriber rollback stale turn

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- When workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn retains a session_submit failsafe after SubmitAsync timeout, HTTP 503, or backend_unavailable, the Codex/plugin wrapper does not throw Plugin command failed with exit code 1.
- The caller receives a retryable degraded/queued envelope with persisted false, degraded true, queued true, and the failsafe path, matching the existing command_timeout contract.
- current-turn.yaml stays in_progress with the updated turn fields and is not rolled back.
- A second updateTurn for the same requestId while that failsafe is queued does not create another session_submit yaml for the same payload.
- A later successful persist or failsafe drain submits the turn once and then removes the queued record.
Implementation notes:

- The inner persist contract already exists in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-ReplPersistTurn: Write-ReplFailsafe then SubmitAsync; timeout/503 sets LastReplPersistenceDetails and returns false without throwing. The gap is the wrapper boundary: Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn does not surface those details, script-entry maps false to exit 1, and plugins/core/lib-ps/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 throws on any nonzero child exit.

- Reuse the command_timeout envelope already emitted by Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 (type error, code command_timeout or a persist-degraded equivalent, retryable true, details.degraded/queued true) instead of a new ad-hoc stderr string. completeTurn already prints degraded details only when persist returns true; updateTurn never prints them.

- Write-ReplFailsafe always creates a new {stamp}-session_submit-{random}.yaml. Deduplicate by requestId (or skip a second write while an in-flight/queued record exists for that turn) so retry-after-false-failure cannot enqueue duplicate SubmitAsync payloads.

- Cover the process boundary in Pester, not only the inner return-false path from TEST-MCP-195: invoke updateTurn through Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1/Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 with a stubbed 503 and assert exit/envelope plus a single failsafe file.
description: workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn writes current-turn.yaml first, then Invoke-ReplPersistTurn writes a unique session_submit failsafe and calls client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync. On timeout/HTTP 503/backend_unavailable, persist returns false with degraded/queued details and keeps the failsafe, but does not emit that contract. Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn treats the false as failure, repl-invoke.ps1 exits 1, and Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 throws Plugin command failed with exit code 1. That unclassified throw is indistinguishable from a rejected update, so a retry writes another timestamped failsafe and risks duplicate SubmitAsync replay. This violates FR-MCP-171, which requires the same retryable degraded/queued envelope as the existing command_timeout path and forbids throwing.
BUG-TRIAGE-213.title: Do not exit 1 when updateTurn queues a session_submit failsafe

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- A valid workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn payload that omits queryTitle and has empty or missing current-turn queryText must exit 0.
- The persisted live turn must receive the submitted response, interpretation, tags, and contextList on MCP, not only a leftover session_submit failsafe.
- New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest must accept empty QueryText without ParameterBindingValidationException.
- Regression coverage must run the real persist/upsert path (not MCP_PLUGIN_PERSIST_LOG) with current-turn.yaml that has queryTitle but no queryText.
Implementation notes:
- Mirror the Title fix in plugins/core/lib-ps/McpPluginShim.psm1: add [AllowEmptyString()] to QueryText on New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest.
- In Invoke-ReplTurnUpsertParams, fall back to cached queryTitle when Get-ReplCurrentTurnQueryText and the persist Title are empty; do not bind Mandatory QueryText to ''.
- Server DTOs already treat QueryText as nullable and NormalizeTurn fills it from QueryTitle, so empty QueryText should be omitted or filled rather than rejected at the plugin bind.
- completeTurn uses the same upsert helper and has the same empty-QueryText hole.
description: workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn is handled locally in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 and then persisted through Invoke-ReplPersistTurn -> Invoke-ReplTurnUpsertParams -> New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest. QueryText is [Parameter(Mandatory)][string] with no AllowEmptyString, unlike Title which was already fixed for the same ParameterBindingValidationException (TR-MCP-REPL-018). updateTurn omits Title unless queryTitle is explicit, and QueryText is recovered only from current-turn.yaml then that empty Title. A valid model update (response, tags, contextList) therefore throws, the wrapper returns false (exit 1), and the live MCP turn is not patched. Persist-log tests never exercise this path; the STRICTCOUNT fixture even omits queryText and short-circuits before upsert. A session_submit failsafe can remain from write-ahead persist or an earlier beginTurn, but it is not a successful live-turn update.
BUG-TRIAGE-214.title: updateTurn persist fails on empty QueryText binding

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- user-prompt-submit returns within the default 30s sessionlog timeout after writing session_submit failsafe, with either a durable persist receipt or degraded queued=true and failsafePath set

- A Codex-hosted user-prompt-submit writes pending failsafe YAML under .mcpServer/failsafe/Codex/workspaces/<workspace-key>/pending, not GrokCode, even when the parent PowerShell.Mcp process has PLUGIN_AGENT_NAME or MCP_AGENT_NAME=GrokCode
- Failsafe params.sessionLog.sourceType and sessionId stay Codex and match the Codex runtime; inherited Grok env must not select the agent path segment

- A hung or silent mcpserver-repl SubmitAsync (blocked stdin copy, unclosed stdout, or filled stderr) cannot keep the hook process alive past the method timeout; the session_submit file remains on disk
Implementation notes:

- Open-PluginTurn -> workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn -> Invoke-ReplPersistTurn already writes the failsafe then calls SubmitAsync; the existing timeout/503 degraded path in repl-invoke.ps1 is unreachable if SubmitAsync never returns
- Bound the entire SubmitAsync child lifetime, including Process.Start, stdin CopyTo, and StandardInput.Close, not only ReadToEndAsync.Wait; on timeout keep the in-flight failsafe and return queued

- Get-McpFailsafeAgentSegment in resolve-cache-dir.ps1 ranks PLUGIN_AGENT_NAME ahead of MCP_AGENT_NAME; plugin-env.ps1 sets MCP_AGENT_NAME from HostName but does not clear inherited PLUGIN_AGENT_NAME. Derive the failsafe agent segment from the canonical Codex host/session source type, not leftover parent env
- Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 and PowerShell.Mcp invocations inherit the caller environment; do not let a Grok parent pin the Codex hook's failsafe tree
description: Codex plugin 1.106.0 lib/user-prompt-submit.ps1 opened req-20260916T103908Z-prompt-143b, wrote a valid client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync failsafe, then did not return (observed 99s, required cancel). The YAML payload is Codex (sourceType Codex, sessionId Codex-20260911T180443Z-plugin-session, codex.exe 0.153.4) but the pending path is .mcpServer/failsafe/GrokCode/workspaces/... because Get-McpFailsafeAgentSegment prefers inherited PLUGIN_AGENT_NAME/MCP_AGENT_NAME over the Codex host/session. After Write-ReplFailsafe, Invoke-ReplPersistTurn blocks in Invoke-ReplRaw SubmitAsync; the 30s method timeout never bounded the hook (stdin CopyTo/StandardInput.Close are untimed; PowerShell.Mcp outer stderr redirect can also stall the child after repl starts). Expected: return within the short sessionlog timeout with a persisted or degraded queued receipt, and queue under the Codex failsafe namespace.
