BUG-TRIAGE-226.note: S0: rollback wording is superseded by effective FR-MCP-173. Ordinary sessionlog.* writes bypass the coordinator. Closeout is proof. Do not mark done until H-done AGREE.
technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Calling sessionlog_complete_turn (or POST /mcpserver/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/complete) on an already completed turn with the same requestId and an additive payload persists the merge and returns success when the subscriber is healthy.
- A second complete_turn after a prior successful complete of that turn (compaction-style additive update) also persists and returns success when the subscriber is healthy.

- When subscriber commit is rejected after the local upsert, the client response includes the structured TransactionFailureReason and whether rollback completed; it must not be only the generic 'Subscriber commit failed.' string classified as internal_server_error.
- SubscriberUnavailable and CommitTimeout on this path are classified retryable (not retryable=false internal_server_error).

- After a rejected subscriber commit, the turn graph matches the pre-mutation state (already-completed turn and its children unchanged), and a later retry of the same complete_turn succeeds once the subscriber accepts the commit.
Implementation notes:

- Path: FwhMcpTools.SessionLog.SessionLogCompleteTurn -> SessionLogController.FinalizeTurnAsync -> SessionLogService.UpsertTurnAsync -> TransactionGatedSessionLogService.ExecuteMutationAsync('sessionlog.upsert_turn') -> TurnTransactionCoordinator.ExecuteAsync -> CommitDiffgramAsync. Failure at TurnTransactionCoordinator.cs around the 'Subscriber commit failed.' return; exception text at TransactionGatedSessionLogService.ToTransactionException; tool/REST envelope at McpErrorClassifier.

- Do not treat already-completed turns as immutable on the REST/MCP complete_turn path; additive merge on reopen is intentional. Fix commit confirmation, reason surfacing, and error classification rather than rejecting the second complete.
- Include commit.Reason in Failure/ToTransactionException. Classify coordinator failures separately from generic 500, with retryable=true for SubscriberUnavailable and CommitTimeout.
- Add a TEST-MCP-161-style UpsertTurnAsync commit-fail test (missing today) plus a healthy-subscriber test that completes the same requestId twice with an additive post-compaction payload.

- The reported txn did not include the subscriber reason. Investigate timeout, subscriber unavailable, stale sequence, and hash/decrypt mismatch on large post-compaction turnJson. CaptureSessionAsync snapshots the entire session graph (all turns and children) before every upsert; a long session can delay mutation before commit even though the diffgram body is only the TurnPayload.
description: sessionlog_complete_turn is a supported additive upsert (FR-SUPPORT-014): CompleteTurn sets status=completed and calls UpsertTurnAsync, which merges onto an existing turn including one that is already completed. TransactionGatedSessionLogService gates that as sessionlog.upsert_turn. The coordinator applies the local mutation, then subscriber CommitDiffgramAsync is rejected; Failure() hardcodes 'Subscriber commit failed.', rollback of the pre-image session graph succeeds, and ToTransactionException surfaces exactly the reported message. McpErrorClassifier then maps that InvalidOperationException to non-retryable internal_server_error (500), dropping TransactionFailureReason (SubscriberUnavailable, CommitTimeout, StaleSequence, hash/decrypt mismatch, and so on). Post-compaction reopen-and-complete is the documented stateless lifecycle (begin reopens, complete merges). Rollback means the earlier completed turn is preserved and the additive compaction update is lost. TEST-MCP-161 covers submit/replace/delete commit-fail rollback, not UpsertTurnAsync, which is the complete_turn path.
BUG-TRIAGE-226.title: sessionlog_complete_turn subscriber commit fails on post-compaction additive reopen

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- After sessionlog_open succeeds for a new Codex (or any agent) session, sessionlog_begin_turn with a valid requestId and planFile/todoId (including None/None) persists an in_progress turn and returns success without internal_server_error.

- A DbUpdateException during begin_turn is classified as persistence_error or conflict with details.inner set to the provider text, retryable only for SQLITE_BUSY, and is never returned as internal_server_error with the raw EF saving-entity-changes message.

- If SessionLogTurns is missing PlanFile or TodoId (or other required turn columns), begin_turn fails closed with pending_migration before SaveChanges, matching the SessionLogs agent-header guard used by open/query.
- A UNIQUE constraint on SessionLogTurns (SessionLogId, RequestId) during begin_turn is retried as an update of the existing turn, the same way SubmitAsync retries SessionLogs UNIQUE races.
Implementation notes:

- Primary persist path: FwhMcpTools.SessionLogBeginTurn -> UpsertLifecycleTurnToolAsync -> SessionLogService.UpsertTurnAsync -> _db.SaveChangesAsync. Open path: OpenSessionAsync -> SubmitAsync (schema guard, SaveChangesBudgetedAsync, UNIQUE retry).

- REST gap: SessionLogController.UpsertLifecycleTurnAsync catches only ArgumentException and InvalidOperationException. SubmitAsync also catches DbUpdateException. An uncaught DbUpdateException becomes HTTP 500 internal_server_error retryable=false via GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware fallback/detail sanitization.

- Schema gap: SessionLogSchemaGuard probes only SessionLogs AgentSession header columns. SessionLogTurns.PlanFile and TodoId are required (SQLite snapshot unique index SessionLogId+RequestId). QueryAsync maps missing header columns to SessionLogSchemaPendingMigrationException; UpsertTurnAsync does not.

- Happy-path coverage already exists in SessionLogLifecycleToolErrorTests.SessionLogBeginTurn_NoneNone_ReturnsSuccess on an in-memory EnsureCreated schema. Add a SQLite predecessor-schema test (open succeeds, begin must not 500) and a REST BeginTurn DbUpdateException envelope test.
- Do not treat this as a requestId format bug: req-20260916T170000Z-commit-valhalla-dependency matches SessionLogIdentifierValidator.
description: sessionlog_open persists only the SessionLogs row and succeeds. The immediately following sessionlog_begin_turn inserts the first SessionLogTurns row via UpsertTurnAsync and dies at SaveChanges with a non-retryable 500. Unlike SubmitAsync (used by open), UpsertTurnAsync does not run SessionLogSchemaGuard, does not retry UNIQUE races, and uses raw SaveChangesAsync. REST BeginTurn/UpsertLifecycleTurnAsync also does not catch DbUpdateException, so the EF message An error occurred while saving the entity changes escapes as internal_server_error retryable=false. The first-turn-after-open shape matches a SessionLogTurns schema or constraint failure that SessionLogs-only open never hits, especially missing PlanFile/TodoId columns (required, migration AddSessionLogTurnPlanFileAndTodoId) which the schema guard never probes.
BUG-TRIAGE-229.title: sessionlog_begin_turn SaveChanges fails after successful sessionlog_open

BUG-TRIAGE-232.note: S0: rollback wording is superseded by effective FR-MCP-173. Ordinary sessionlog.* writes bypass the coordinator. Closeout is proof. Do not mark done until H-done AGREE.
technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- sessionlog_begin_turn for a new Codex requestId persists an in_progress turn in the target workspace session log and returns success when subscriber commit confirms.

- When subscriber commit does not confirm, begin_turn fails, the in_progress turn is not left persisted, and the exception includes transaction id plus the structured commit.Reason rather than only Subscriber commit failed. Rollback completed.
- Consecutive mutating session-log operations (commit-sync then begin_turn) either both persist or both fail with that structured reason.
Implementation notes:

- Keep the named path: FwhMcpTools sessionlog_begin_turn -> ISessionLogService.UpsertTurnAsync -> TransactionGatedSessionLogService ExecuteMutationAsync("sessionlog.upsert_turn") -> TurnTransactionCoordinator.ExecuteAsync.

- Do not treat successful rollback as the defect; rollback is intended compensation after a non-committed/non-duplicate DiffgramCommitResponse. The defect is that begin_turn cannot persist because subscriber commit does not confirm.
- Surface commit.Reason in ToTransactionException (TransactionGatedSessionLogService) instead of replacing it with the generic Subscriber commit failed message.

- Inspect subscriber commit for the failing txn: timeout (CommitTimeoutSeconds), HTTP/direct pub-sub SubscriberUnavailable, and InMemorySubscriberCommitService rejects. Sequence is per gated-service instance (unix milliseconds) while lastSequence is global per publisher/subscriber pair with Sequence <= lastSequence as StaleSequence.
description: sessionlog_begin_turn maps to TransactionGatedSessionLogService.UpsertTurnAsync (operation sessionlog.upsert_turn). The turn mutation is applied, then TurnTransactionCoordinator.CommitDiffgramAsync must return committed or duplicate. Any other subscriber status triggers compensation with a generic Subscriber commit failed message and, when rollback succeeds, the exception Turn transaction coordinator did not commit sessionlog.upsert_turn '{txn}': Subscriber commit failed. Rollback completed. That matches txn-462e9f7d4be2483c9177565b406cbbd4 for req-20260916T184316Z-vice-sharp-readme on NeuralNetworks. The in-progress Codex turn is not persisted. The same post-mutation commit failure was reported on the preceding commit-sync turn, so this is a repeated subscriber-commit reject, not a one-off rollback bug. ToTransactionException currently prefers that generic Message and omits commit.Reason (CommitTimeout, SubscriberUnavailable, StaleSequence, ReplayNonce, hash/decrypt mismatch, DuplicateConflict).
BUG-TRIAGE-232.title: sessionlog_begin_turn rolls back when subscriber commit fails

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- After the active session-log turn is already completed (workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn or sessionlog_complete_turn succeeded), stop-gate must not emit decision=block with reason 'stale cached session cannot be reused for <requestId>'.

- A session-state.yaml timestamp or lastUpdated older than 24 hours must not by itself block stop when current-turn.yaml is missing, status=completed, or its turnRequestId is not the in-progress turn.
- The block reason must not cite a stale pinned current-turn.yaml requestId that is unrelated to the turn that was just completed.

- Pester seeds session-state.yaml with timestamp/lastUpdated older than 24 hours and current-turn.yaml status=completed (plus a variant whose pinned turnRequestId differs from the completed server request) and asserts stop-gate returns allow/empty JSON with no stale-cache block.
Implementation notes:

- The defect is the 24h short-circuit in Close-PluginTurnIfNeeded in plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1 (the 'stale cached session cannot be reused' Write-PluginJson). stop-gate.ps1 is only the generated wrapper; change the shared hook function.

- Move or drop that check so completed/absent current turns fall through to the existing allow path. Align with Open-PluginTurn, which refreshes lastUpdated on the same age condition instead of blocking.
- Prefer lastUpdated for recency. Do not treat a static session-start timestamp as proof the live session cannot be reused.
- If MCP-tool completeTurn can close the server turn without rewriting plugin current-turn.yaml, stop-gate must still allow when the local pin is stale rather than blocking on that pin.
description: Close-PluginTurnIfNeeded (plugin-hook.ps1, invoked as stop-gate) hard-blocks when session-state.yaml timestamp or lastUpdated is older than 24 hours, before it inspects current-turn.yaml status. After sessionlog_complete_turn successfully completed req-20260917T120934Z-diagnose-full-suite-hang (turn 45181) in Codex-20260915T201211Z-r0-parity, stop-gate still emitted decision=block with 'stale cached session cannot be reused for req-20260916T103908Z-prompt-143b'. That requestId is read from the local current-turn.yaml pin and is unrelated to the completed server turn. Open-PluginTurn already refreshes lastUpdated on the same 24h condition and continues; stop-gate does not. There is no Pester coverage of this 24h short-circuit.
BUG-TRIAGE-234.title: Stop gate blocks completed turns on a stale session-state timestamp

BUG-TRIAGE-236.note: S0: rollback wording is superseded by effective FR-MCP-173. Ordinary sessionlog.* writes bypass the coordinator. Closeout is proof. Do not mark done until H-done AGREE.
technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- sessionlog_begin_turn on an existing session either commits sessionlog.upsert_turn (committed or duplicate) or returns a classified error that includes the subscriber commit.Reason (timeout, subscriber unavailable, hash mismatch, stale sequence, replay nonce, decrypt failure, or duplicate conflict).
- When subscriber commit fails, the local session-log mutation stays rolled back: no orphan in_progress turn remains for that sessionId and requestId.
- Subscriber unavailability and commit timeout are not classified as nonretryable internal_server_error.
Implementation notes:

- Do not merge with Keyserver manifest signing failed reports: those fail in SignManifestAsync before mutation (mutationApplied false). This report is the later CommitDiffgramAsync reject/timeout/unavailable path.

- TurnTransactionCoordinator.ExecuteAsync discards commit.Reason and always emits Subscriber commit failed. Preserve Reason (and DiffgramCommitResponse.Message if present) in TurnTransactionResult.Message so ToTransactionException can surface it.

- McpErrorClassifier.Classify falls through generic InvalidOperationException to InternalError retryable false. Map TransactionFailureReason.CommitTimeout and SubscriberUnavailable to retryable timeout/backend-style codes.

- Investigate live subscriber reject cause for txn-0c488a1a6c48404d861edbdecaa5a2ea: InMemorySubscriberCommitService can reject on verify failure, encrypted-body hash mismatch, decrypt failure, stale sequence, replay nonce, or duplicate conflict; the coordinator also maps publish exceptions to SubscriberUnavailable and commit deadline to CommitTimeout.
description: Native sessionlog_begin_turn for Codex-20260915T201211Z-r0-parity / req-20260917T134022Z-existing-gigdriving-app failed as nonretryable internal_server_error. The tool upserts an in_progress turn through TransactionGatedSessionLogService.UpsertTurnAsync (operation sessionlog.upsert_turn). TurnTransactionCoordinator signs the manifest, applies the session-log mutation, then CommitDiffgramAsync via pub-sub/subscriber did not return committed or duplicate for txn-0c488a1a6c48404d861edbdecaa5a2ea. The coordinator always replaces the structured commit.Reason with the generic message Subscriber commit failed., rolls back the mutation, and TransactionGatedSessionLogService throws InvalidOperationException (Rollback completed.). McpErrorClassifier maps that InvalidOperationException to retryable=false internal_server_error, so clients do not retry even for timeout or subscriber-unavailable. This is the post-mutation subscriber-commit stage of FR-MCP-120, not the earlier Keyserver manifest signing failed path (mutation never applied). Deduplicate only with other Subscriber commit failed. Rollback completed. reports.
BUG-TRIAGE-236.title: sessionlog_begin_turn rolls back after subscriber commit failure

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- After session-start recovery or sessionId rotation that rebinds current-turn.yaml, workflow.sessionlog.appendActions on that rebound turn returns success and does not return HTTP 400 'Invalid session turn planFile/todoId: planFile is omitted'.
- workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn with planFile and todoId in params includes those exact values on the SubmitAsync turn payload and does not omit planFile.
- When current-turn.yaml has planFile: None and todoId: None, incremental persist sends the sentinel string None (not a missing property) so a rebound turn is accepted as a new entry.
- A failed appendActions/updateTurn caused by omitted planFile does not leave a pending session_submit failsafe YAML for that call.
Implementation notes:

- Defect is in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1: Invoke-WorkflowAppendActions and Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn call Invoke-ReplPersistTurn without -PlanFile/-TodoId. Only beginTurn passes those fields.

- Assert-ReplCurrentTurnFresh (TR-MCP-PLUGIN-012) rewrites current-turn.yaml sessionId onto the recovered session, then SubmitAsync applies ValidateForNewEntry because that requestId is not on the new session.

- Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn currently copies only response, interpretation, tokenCount, tags, and contextList from params. It must also accept planFile/todoId, write them to current-turn.yaml, and pass them through persist.

- New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest in plugins/core/lib-ps/McpPluginShim.psm1 only serializes planFile/todoId when non-empty. Incremental persist must supply the cache values or the None sentinel rather than relying on omitted-field merge.
- Do not weaken ValidateForNewEntry. First persist of a rebound turn on a recovered session is a new entry and must keep required planFile/todoId.
description: Plugin 1.107.0 session-start recovery mints a new sessionId and rebinds leftover current-turn.yaml onto that session. workflow.sessionlog.appendActions and updateTurn then persist via client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync without PlanFile/TodoId. New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest drops empty values, so the turn payload omits planFile. Submit treats the rebound requestId as a new turn and SessionLogTurnContextValidator.ValidateForNewEntry returns HTTP 400 'planFile is omitted'. current-turn.yaml already had planFile: None, and an explicit updateTurn planFile/todoId is ignored because updateTurn never reads those params. Two session_submit failsafe files are the expected side effect of those failed persists.
BUG-TRIAGE-239.title: Session log persist omits planFile after recovered-session rebind

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- When workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog persist times out or returns HTTP 503 backend_unavailable, the plugin emits a classified diagnostic (code, retryable, degraded, queued, method, failsafe retained) on stdout or stderr before returning. Empty stdout plus empty stderr is a failure.

- Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 must not surface that case as an unclassified 'Plugin command failed with exit code 1' that drops child stderr. Either include child stderr in the wrapper error or emit the same classified YAML envelope used for wrapper command_timeout.

- Retryable appendDialog persist failure retains the failsafe, leaves current-turn in_progress, and does not block the caller the way a hard persist failure does. Align with beginTurn degraded/queued success, or keep exit 1 only when the classified diagnostic from criterion 1 is present.

- mcp-status / failsafe.status identifies the queued method as written (client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync versus client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync) so a leftover session_submit record is distinguishable from an appendDialog failsafe.
- A successful appendDialog still uses client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync and does not fall back to a full-session client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync upsert (TEST-MCP-195).
Implementation notes:

- Fix site 1: Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog timeout/503 branch in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 currently sets LastReplPersistenceDetails and returns false with no [Console]::Error.WriteLine. Script-entry then exit 1 with no stdout.
- Fix site 2: plugins/core/lib-ps/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 copies child stderr to Console.Error then throws using stdout only. On empty stdout the throw is a generic exit-code message.

- Do not retarget appendDialog onto SubmitAsync. PersistTurn still writes method client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync label session_submit before the call; appendDialog writes AppendDialogAsync label session_dialog. Reconcile both queue shapes.

- beginTurn already documents the desired degrade contract: Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist returns success with stderr 'queued/degraded' and keeps current-turn active. Reuse that pattern or the wrapper command_timeout envelope (type: error, code: command_timeout, retryable: true, degraded/queued).

- Cover with a Pester case: stub AppendDialogAsync timeout/503, assert classified diagnostic is visible through Invoke-McpPlugin, failsafe remains, current-turn stays in_progress, and SubmitAsync is not invoked.
description: workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog is a local shim in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1. On success or failure it emits no stdout (boolean output is suppressed). Script-entry then exits 1 whenever LastInvokeReplMethodSuccess is false. The timeout/HTTP 503 branch queues a failsafe and returns false without writing stderr, so Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 sees a non-zero child with empty stdout and throws only 'Plugin command failed with exit code 1' (stderr is not copied into that throw). That matches empty diagnostics while model work continues. Retryable persist is inconsistent with beginTurn, which treats timeout/503 as degraded/queued success and keeps current-turn active. A pending client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync record is written by Invoke-ReplPersistTurn (beginTurn/updateTurn/completeTurn) before the upsert; current appendDialog failsafe is client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync. The observed SubmitAsync item is leftover persist-queue state that still needs drain/reconciliation, not proof that appendDialog itself submitted a full session.
BUG-TRIAGE-240.title: appendDialog persist failure exits 1 with empty stdout and a queued failsafe

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- When appendDialog or completeTurn persist times out or returns HTTP 503, the plugin wrapper surfaces a structured failure that includes degraded=true, queued=true, the failsafe path or pendingCount, and the persist message. It must not throw only Plugin command failed with exit code 1.
- On that failure the current turn stays in_progress, the failsafe record remains pending (not quarantined), and workflow.failsafe.status reports pendingCount greater than 0.
- After a successful failsafe drain or retry, completeTurn marks the turn completed and QueryAsync still returns the verified review body.
- A non-zero plugin exit includes child stderr (and any LastReplPersistenceDetails message) in the wrapper error payload, not only stdout.
Implementation notes:

- plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog timeout/503 branch writes failsafe and returns false with no Console.Error line. Invoke-WorkflowCompleteTurn also returns false with no diagnostic when Invoke-ReplPersistTurn returns false; the degraded message is emitted only after a successful persist.
- plugins/core/lib-ps/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 appends stdout to the thrown exit-code message and omits stderr, so even written diagnostics are dropped if the host only catches the exception.

- Recover the existing queued session_submit/session_dialog record with failsafe drain, then retry completeTurn against the same requestId and confirm server status. Do not treat the already-verified QueryAsync body as lost.
description: A 12834-character Nashville review body was already confirmed on the server via QueryAsync. The following workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog/completeTurn sequence failed with only Plugin command failed with exit code 1. Live status was available with pendingCount 1, failsafeCount 1, quarantine 0, and the turn was still unclaimed. That matches the plugin degrade path: repl-invoke.ps1 writes a failsafe record then returns false and exits 1 without printing the persist message, while Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 throws using stdout only and drops stderr. The queued record is retained; completion is not durable until drain/retry succeeds.
BUG-TRIAGE-241.title: Session-log wrapper exits 1 with no diagnostic when appendDialog/completeTurn persist is queued

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- When workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn persist times out or returns HTTP 503, the wrapper still exits non-zero if the requested title was not persisted.
- The same failure emits a non-empty diagnostic (stderr or result body) that states degraded/queued persist and includes the failsafe path.
- failsafe.status reports the queued session_submit YAML after that failure.
- A live sessionlog query after the failed update still shows the previous title; a later updateTurn retry persists the requested title once the backend accepts SubmitAsync.
- Other MCP surfaces (for example requirements) remain usable during the transient persist failure.
Implementation notes:
- Treat the Nashville incident as a transient SubmitAsync timeout or 503, not a workspace outage. Do not implement product work from the failed call.
- In Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn, on a false return from Invoke-ReplPersistTurn, emit LastReplPersistenceDetails the same way Invoke-WorkflowCompleteTurn already does (message plus FailsafePath).
- Local workflow methods currently write no stdout by design; diagnostics must go to stderr or a structured result body the host actually surfaces.
- Keep the failsafe-first persist path. Do not clear the queued submit on timeout. Do not retitle the session from an incidental retry unless the caller explicitly set the turn title.
description: workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn failed once during Nashville planning after about 17 seconds, left the previous turn title in place, queued one failsafe YAML, and succeeded on retry while requirements calls stayed healthy. In plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1, Invoke-ReplPersistTurn always queues client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync, then on timeout or HTTP 503 returns false without writing a diagnostic. Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn forwards that false; unlike beginTurn and completeTurn it does not emit LastReplPersistenceDetails. The script entry then exits 1 with empty stdout, so the host surfaces no error body even though failsafe.status correctly shows the queued record.
BUG-TRIAGE-243.title: sessionlog updateTurn persist timeout exits 1 with empty body

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:
- An isolated workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog then updateTurn closure whose primary persist times out or returns HTTP 503/backend_unavailable does not exit 1 with empty stderr.
- When failsafe session_submit is retained, the command either exits 0 as degraded success or exits non-zero with stderr naming the method, requestId, failsafe path, and reason.
- A live in_progress request whose response is still the 13-character beginTurn placeholder '(turn opened)' is reported as not durably updated.
Implementation notes:

- plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn returns Invoke-ReplPersistTurn's false on the timeout/503 branch; that branch sets LastReplPersistenceDetails but never WriteLine, and script-entry then exit 1.
- Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog timeout/503 writes label session_dialog and also returns false with no stderr; the reported session_submit label is the PersistTurn path used by updateTurn.
- Align updateTurn (and appendDialog) with Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn: on LastReplPersistenceDetails.degraded/queued, write the failsafe diagnostic and return true per FR-MCP-REPL-009 AC1.
- Do not treat this as a parent-turn or product-write defect; the reporter did not attempt those writes.
description: Isolated reviewer closure via workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog then updateTurn did not persist. Invoke-ReplPersistTurn writes a session_submit failsafe, then on timeout or HTTP 503 backend_unavailable returns false without throwing. Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn forwards that false with no Console.Error line, so repl-invoke script-entry exits 1 with empty stdout/stderr. The live request stays in_progress with the beginTurn placeholder '(turn opened)' (13 characters). FR-MCP-REPL-009 requires update and appendDialog to remain successful when failsafe succeeds; beginTurn already returns true and writes a queued/degraded diagnostic on the same persist path.
BUG-TRIAGE-244.title: updateTurn persist degrade exits 1 with empty stderr

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- After UserPromptSubmit beginTurn for a request such as req-20260923T164803Z-prompt-ccb9 is queued to failsafe following a healthy marker rewrite, current-turn.yaml remains status in_progress and still contains the original queryText and queryTitle.
- workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn on that turn succeeds, and the server turn with the same requestId is queryable with that same queryText, without replaying beginTurn.
- An updateTurn persist does not store an empty queryText over a server turn that already has query text.
- While the begin payload is still only in the failsafe queue, updateTurn does not fail for a missing planFile or todoId that the queued begin payload already captured.
Implementation notes:

- Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 replaces the full current-turn.yaml from Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn with a three-field stub. Keep queryText, queryTitle, openedAt, planFile, todoId, and the marker snapshot on the degraded in_progress cache.

- Invoke-ReplTurnUpsertParams copies query text only from the cache, then from Title. Invoke-WorkflowUpdateTurn leaves Title empty unless queryTitle is passed, and ReplYamlMessageValidator does not allow queryText on workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn. Omit an empty queryText from the SubmitAsync payload so SessionLogService.ApplyValue does not treat "" as supplied.

- The begin failsafe record is written before the stub overwrite and already contains queryText, planFile, and todoId. Replay that record before the update submit, or copy those fields onto the update payload.
- BeginTurn.SubmitTimeoutAfterFailsafe_ReturnsDegradedQueued only checks the stub fields. Extend it so a degraded begin keeps queryText.
description: After a healthy marker rewrite, UserPromptSubmit calls workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn. When SubmitAsync is queued to failsafe (timeout or HTTP 503), beginTurn still returns success and Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist rewrites current-turn.yaml to only turnRequestId, sessionId, and status in_progress, dropping queryText and queryTitle. The begin failsafe record still has the prompt, but workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn does not accept queryText, omits queryTitle unless that call sets it, and submits queryText as an empty string. If the server turn is not created yet, that submit is a first persist with no planFile or todoId and SessionLogTurnContextValidator.ValidateForNewEntry rejects it. If the turn already exists, ApplyValue treats the empty queryText as supplied and clears the stored query. Replaying beginTurn is the only path that writes queryText again.
BUG-TRIAGE-245.title: Degraded Codex beginTurn drops query text and blocks updateTurn

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- After beginTurn persist times out or returns degraded, a later beginTurn for the same requestId that supplies only requestId, queryTitle, and queryText is accepted and stores planFile and todoId as None, or as the values captured before the failed persist.
- That recovery submit does not return HTTP 400 validation_error for omitted planFile or todoId.
- A beginTurn for a requestId that is already durably stored still omits planFile and todoId so the stored pair is left unchanged.
- A first persist that reaches the server with both fields omitted still returns HTTP 400 validation_error, except a canceled or cancelled supersede persist, which stamps None and succeeds.

- The beginTurn examples in docs/context/module-bootstrap.md and docs/REPL-USER-GUIDE.md, and the required params in docs/context/repl-yaml-message.schema.json, state that first persist requires planFile and todoId and that None is the sentinel when there is no plan or TODO.
Implementation notes:

- Do not classify a degraded, never-persisted beginTurn as a same-requestId reopen. Stamp planFile and todoId before SubmitAsync: use the values written on the failed attempt, otherwise the exact sentinel None.

- Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 rewrites current-turn.yaml without planFile and todoId. Keep those fields on the degraded turn file so recovery can resubmit them.
- New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest in plugins/core/lib-ps/McpPluginShim.psm1 omits blank planFile and todoId. A recovery payload must set both before that helper runs.

- Server rule stays in SessionLogTurnContextValidator.ValidateForNewEntry and SessionLogService.ApplyTurnContext. Only IsSupersededHookPersist may stamp None when status is canceled or cancelled. Do not relax first-persist validation for in_progress turns.

- Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn already defaults blanks to None when current-turn.yaml does not already hold that requestId. plugins/core/test-fixtures/pester/SessionLogTurnContextBeginTurn.Tests.ps1 covers that default and the durable reopen omission. Add a degraded-retry case that expects None/None on the second persist.
description: workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn documents requestId, queryTitle, and queryText as the required params. On a real first persist, Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn stamps omitted planFile and todoId to the exact sentinel None before client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync. SessionLogService.ApplyTurnContext calls ValidateForNewEntry for any turn that is not already stored, and an omitted field becomes HTTP 400 validation_error. After a timed-out or HTTP 503 beginTurn, Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist leaves current-turn.yaml active with only turnRequestId, sessionId, and status. TR-MCP-REPL-016.description: BUG-TRIAGE-097. The plugin PowerShell runtime captures every session-log submit into the failsafe queue before the remote call but never replays it, so records accumulate forever (33 on disk in F:/GitHub/McpServer, oldest 2026-07-14). plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 MUST expose Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrain, which walks the failsafe directory oldest-first (the file name is prefixed with the UTC capture stamp, so a name sort is a chronological sort) and re-issues each record's captured method and params through Invoke-ReplRaw. A record MUST be deleted only after its submission succeeds; a record whose submission fails MUST stay on disk. client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync is an upsert keyed by sessionId plus requestId, so a replay is idempotent. A record rejected by the backend MUST NOT block the newer records behind it: the drain increments that record's drainAttempts counter and continues the walk. A transport-level failure (MCP_UNTRUSTED, mcpserver-repl not on PATH, timeout, refused connection) MUST abort the pass without consuming any attempt budget, because the backend and not the record is at fault. The drain MUST skip the record belonging to the submit currently in flight, so a drain triggered inside an active submit cannot double-submit or delete the live turn. The drain MUST be wired to the first successful Invoke-ReplRaw in the process (Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrainOnFirstSuccess, latched to run at most once and disabled by MCP_FAILSAFE_DRAIN_DISABLED=1) rather than to bootstrap: bootstrap only proves the marker file is fresh, does not prove the backend answers, and runs inside Invoke-ReplRaw, so draining there would recurse. Operators MUST be able to force a full pass with the plugin-local verb workflow.failsafe.drain (optional maxRecords and maxAttempts params), which prints the drain summary as YAML and exits non-zero only when the pass aborted.
TR-MCP-REPL-016.title: Failsafe queue drains oldest-first after a proven-reachable backend call

TR-MCP-REPL-017.description: BUG-TRIAGE-097. A failsafe record that cannot be replayed MUST be quarantined rather than retried forever or deleted, because a captured record can be the only copy of a turn. plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 MUST move a record to a quarantine subdirectory of the failsafe directory, next to a sibling .reason.txt naming the quarantine timestamp, the original path, and the reason, when the record is not readable YAML, when its root is not a mapping, when it has no method or no params, or when its drainAttempts counter has reached the attempt budget (default 5). Quarantined records MUST NOT be counted as live queue depth. plugins/core/lib-ps/resolve-cache-dir.ps1 MUST own the single resolution of the queue location (Get-McpFailsafeDir and Get-McpFailsafeQuarantineDir, honouring MCPSERVER_FAILSAFE_DIR then MCP_FAILSAFE_DIR then the workspace cache) so the writer, the drain, and the status reporter cannot disagree. plugins/core/lib-ps/mcp-status.ps1 MUST count the failsafe directory: pendingCount previously counted only the cache pending directory and therefore reported 0 while 33 captured submits sat undrained, so pendingCount MUST be the sum of pending turn records and queued failsafe records, and the status document MUST additionally expose pendingTurnCount, failsafeDir, failsafeCount, and failsafeQuarantineCount. A read-only workflow.failsafe.status verb MUST report the same depth without replaying anything.
TR-MCP-REPL-017.title: Failsafe quarantine and truthful pending queue depth in plugin status
